key_insight: 2D-FET-Bench V2 tests whether language-model agents can reliably turn flake contours and device specs into valid 2D FET layouts, rather than just describing them.
engineering_relevance: This matters for automating layout generation for exfoliated 2D-material devices, where each flake has a unique geometry and hand-drawn device design is slow and error-prone.
method: 128 microscopy-derived layout tasks, including hole-containing and multi-flake cases
Agents output typed polygon and path operations that are rendered to GDSII
A deterministic verifier checks geometric/structural rules, plus a separate contour-integrity check
evidence_signal: Scripted reference layouts pass all 128 tasks, and the best model/workflow in the six-model panel, GPT5.6-Luna with ReAct-3, achieves 62.3% pass rate per attempt, 80.5% task coverage, and 43.8% all-five-attempt consistency.
watch_item: Verifier pass does not guarantee physically optimal or fabrication-ready designs, and expert audit acceptance is only about 56.4% to 63.5% of sampled passed layouts.
paper_title: 2d-fet-bench: from spatial reasoning to fet design on flakes
